title: Bookshop spare room (fictional)
question: How should the neighbourhood bookshop use its spare room for the next three months?
context: Fictional case only. One spare room; decision horizon is the next three months. Shared constraints (apply to every option; not peer choices): one staff member can spare five hours a week; there is no demand data; there is no confirmed budget. Reader edit preserved: workshops must finish by 18:00. User-stated options to compare: paid workshops, a quiet reading room, or keep as storage. A shared timetable is a proposed extension, not proof that every possible use is covered. Recommendation deliberately deferred.
nextQuestion: Want to pressure-test daytime demand under the 18:00 finish rule, or draft a single pilot checklist?

nodes.label: Use of the spare room
nodes.notes: Scoped comparison for the next three months: what is this spare room's primary designated use? Universe: this one room over that horizon. Grouping basis: primary use designation. Option-level partition siblings (options only): (1) paid workshops only, (2) quiet reading room only, (3) keep as storage. These three are the user-stated competing designations and are mutually exclusive as primary use. 'Proposed extensions' is a parking question for extra ideas (e.g. shared timetable); it is not a fourth primary-use option and does not prove the map covers every conceivable use. Shared staff/budget/data limits live in session context and these root notes — not as sibling cards beside options. Excluded for now: permanent rebuild, selling the space, unrelated retail fit-outs. Reader edit preserved: workshops must finish by 18:00.

nodes.label: Paid workshops only
nodes.notes: Primary use: scheduled paid sessions in the room (writing, book clubs with fees, craft-with-books, author events with tickets). Mechanism (proposed): ticket or course fees plus possible book-attach sales convert spare floor into near-term cash and footfall. Hard boundary from reader edit: workshops must finish by 18:00. Competing with reading-room calm and with storage convenience. Proposed alternative, not a recommendation. Staff/budget limits are shared context (five hours/week; no confirmed budget), not separate sibling options.

nodes.label: Must finish by 18:00
nodes.notes: Reader-stated operating rule for this exploration (context/provenance: user edit on the canvas). Workshops under this branch are assumed to end by 18:00. This is a binding design constraint for formats and audience, not market evidence that daytime sessions will sell.
nodes.source: Reader edit on exported HTML: workshops must finish by 18:00.

nodes.label: Locals will pay for sessions
nodes.notes: Assumption, not evidence: neighbourhood residents will book and pay enough to justify clearing the room and the five weekly hours, even with a finish-by-18:00 rule. Counterpoint: interest in free events does not prove paid demand; no demand data is supplied; early finish may exclude after-work adults. Next check: soft-count interest (waitlist, deposit for one pilot theme) before committing the full three months. Do not invent attendance or price figures.

nodes.label: Daytime audience is reachable
nodes.notes: Assumption forced into view by the 18:00 finish rule: enough paying participants can attend before early evening (remote workers, caregivers, retirees, home-based adults). Counterpoint: classic after-work adult workshops may be weakly served. Next check: ask a small customer sample about daytime paid sessions — still no invented numbers.

nodes.label: Five hours covers run-rate
nodes.notes: Assumption: five staff hours/week can sustain a credible workshop cadence (planning, hosting, recovery, light marketing) with sessions finishing by 18:00. Counterpoint: one poorly scoped series can consume the whole allowance with little left for the shop floor; an early finish time may also shrink evening-adult demand. Next check: timebox a single pilot session end-to-end and measure actual hours used.

nodes.label: Promo fits inside five hours
nodes.notes: Assumption: discovery (in-shop posters, email, social, partner shares) can be done inside the same five hours/week as prep and hosting, or via near-zero-extra-effort channels. Counterpoint: empty seats are often a marketing-hours problem. Next check: write a one-pilot promo checklist with minute estimates.

nodes.label: Partner host can add capacity
nodes.notes: Assumption: a local teacher, author or community group could host under the shop's roof, stretching beyond five staff hours. Counterpoint: partners need vetting, revenue share and still require shop oversight before 18:00 close of session. Next check: list two plausible partners and what the shop would still owe in hours.

nodes.label: Setup fits unknown budget
nodes.notes: Assumption: chairs, materials, insurance or guest fees fit within whatever budget is later confirmed. No budget is confirmed yet; treat cost as an open gate, not a known constraint. Next check: list minimum viable setup costs for one pilot before buying anything.

nodes.label: Events won't hurt core retail
nodes.notes: Assumption: using the spare room for paid sessions does not materially damage browse experience, stock access or till coverage during those hours. Counterpoint: noise, blocked storage and staff pulled off floor. Next check: after one pilot, note floor complaints and missed till coverage — qualitative is enough at first.

nodes.label: No demand or price evidence yet
nodes.notes: Evidence gap (explicit): case supplies no historical ticket sales, competitor prices, or waitlist data. Absence of data is not evidence against workshops; it blocks a supported preference.

nodes.label: Which formats to trial
nodes.notes: Deepening question under paid workshops only — not a new room-use option. Grouping basis: session format for a possible workshops-primary use. Siblings are concrete format ideas to explore; they can later combine in a calendar but are listed as distinct format candidates here. No ranking or winner.

nodes.label: Ticketed author / talk events
nodes.notes: Proposed format: paid tickets for author talks or readings finishing by 18:00. Mechanism: event fee + book signing sales. Dependencies: speaker availability daytime/early evening; promo time within five hours. Unverified demand.

nodes.label: Short skills courses
nodes.notes: Proposed format: multi-week or one-off skills sessions (e.g. writing, journaling, bookbinding) with a course fee, ending by 18:00. Mechanism: prepaid seats smooth cashflow. Dependencies: curriculum prep hours vs five-hour cap; materials cost under unknown budget.

nodes.label: Paid book-club sessions
nodes.notes: Proposed format: facilitated book discussion with a session fee, finishing by 18:00. Mechanism: recurring small group; book-attach sales. Dependencies: facilitator time; whether fee feels fair vs free clubs nearby. No local fee evidence yet.

nodes.label: Daytime family / kids craft
nodes.notes: Proposed format: daytime family or kids craft-with-books sessions (fits finish-by-18:00 more naturally than late adult evenings). Mechanism: caregiver spend + kids titles. Dependencies: safeguarding/space rules; mess reset within five hours. Demand unknown.

nodes.label: One pilot before a 3-month bet
nodes.notes: Optional learning step if workshops remain in play — not a decision that workshops win. Design one session ending by 18:00, with a hour log, a minimum setup-cost list, and a soft demand signal (waitlist or deposits). Keep other room-use options open meanwhile.

nodes.label: Quiet reading room only
nodes.notes: Primary use: a calm place to sit and read, possibly with soft dwell cues (seating, light rules, no ticketed events). Mechanism (proposed): longer dwell and goodwill increase browse-and-buy and repeat visits, without charging for the room itself. Trade-off: little or no direct room revenue; needs the room cleared of storage. Proposed alternative, not a recommendation.

nodes.label: Dwell turns into purchases
nodes.notes: Assumption: quieter seating raises time-in-shop and conversion enough to matter over three months. Counterpoint: dwell can rise while sales stay flat; some readers may treat it as a free library. Next check: if trialled, track visits that use the room versus basket size/frequency versus a baseline week — still no invented numbers here.

nodes.label: Five hours keep it inviting
nodes.notes: Assumption: five hours/week suffice for setup, light supervision, cleaning and resetting without becoming a babysitting service. Counterpoint: unsupervised space can create loss, noise or conflict with shop work. Next check: define simple house rules and a supervision model before opening.

nodes.label: No dwell or conversion data
nodes.notes: Evidence gap: no measured dwell time, conversion, or customer requests for a reading corner are supplied. Customer anecdotes would still be weak evidence until counted.

nodes.label: Keep as storage
nodes.notes: Primary use remains stock, seasonal displays, overstock and operational storage — the status-quo / no-customer-facing-change option. Mechanism (proposed): preserves shop-floor efficiency, avoids setup cost and protects the five hours for core retail. Opportunity cost: forgoes learning about workshops or reading-room demand in this three-month window. Proposed alternative, not a recommendation.

nodes.label: Storage scarcity is binding
nodes.notes: Assumption: losing this storage would harm fulfilment, safety or merchandising enough to outweigh upside from customer uses. Counterpoint: some stored stock may be dead or relocatable. Next check: inventory what is stored, what must stay on-site, and what could move or be cleared cheaply.

nodes.label: Waiting preserves option value
nodes.notes: Assumption: with no demand data or budget, delaying a customer-facing fit-out avoids wasted spend and keeps the room flexible. Counterpoint: three months of inaction also yields no demand signal. Next check: if storage wins temporarily, still schedule a cheap signal (survey, one pop-up) so the next decision is better informed.

nodes.label: No cost of storage measured
nodes.notes: Evidence gap: opportunity cost of the room and true necessity of current storage contents are unmeasured.

nodes.label: Proposed extensions
nodes.notes: Not part of the three-way primary-use partition. Parking place for ideas beyond the user-stated options (paid workshops, quiet reading room, keep as storage). Presence of ideas here does not prove collective exhaustiveness of the main comparison. Relationship to parent: reference/parking, not a competing primary-use designation.

nodes.label: Shared timetable (proposed)
nodes.notes: Proposed extension, not one of the three user-stated primary options and not proof of coverage. Idea: clear the room for customers with a published split (e.g. reading room most hours; paid workshops on set evenings, finishing by 18:00). Mechanism (proposed): test both customer uses without a full three-month bet on one. Costs: scheduling friction, reset work, quiet-vs-event conflict — all drawing on the same five hours/week. Keep as an open idea beside the main three-way comparison; do not treat it as evidence the map is collectively exhaustive.

nodes.label: Reset fits five hours
nodes.notes: Assumption: switching the room between quiet seating and workshop layout fits inside five hours/week plus any volunteer help. Counterpoint: dual use can burn the whole allowance on logistics. Next check: draft a weekly timetable and hour budget before promising both.

nodes.label: Split use yields clearer signal
nodes.notes: Assumption: running both lightly for three months produces comparable learning on demand and ops load. Counterpoint: thin attention may under-test both and muddy the signal. Next check: pick one primary metric per use (e.g. paid seats booked vs reading-room visits) and review at a midpoint.

nodes.label: No timetable or staffing plan
nodes.notes: Evidence gap: no draft calendar, reset checklist, or staff roster exists yet for dual use.

decision.rationale: Exploration only. No winner selected. Paid-workshops branch deepened; shared timetable parked under proposed extensions; shared staff/budget limits in context/root notes; option comparison level holds the three user-stated options only.
uncertainties: Paid demand (especially for sessions that finish by 18:00) is unknown.
Whether reading-room dwell would increase purchases is unknown.
Whether current storage contents are truly binding is unknown.
No confirmed budget for setup, materials or insurance.
Whether five hours/week can sustain workshops, a reading room, or a proposed shared timetable is untested.
The three user-stated options do not exhaust every conceivable use; other hybrids remain possible.
nextSteps: Keep the three user-stated options open; treat shared timetable as an optional extension only.
If exploring workshops further: list minimum setup cost and a one-pilot promo/hour checklist under the 18:00 rule.
Inventory what is stored and what must stay on-site.
Choose one cheap demand signal before preferring any room use.
